doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Minton's patrons and Adele's cooking
summary: Politicians and gangsters came to Minton's, partly for the cook Adele, and musicians paid for meals.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, they had all kind of people coming in there. It’s hard to say now. I knew all of them. Adam Clayton Powell...
This is Smalls you’re talking about?

No, this is Minton’s. Malcolm X used to stick his head in the door, but he didn’t come in there. The big gangsters, Bumpy Johnson, all those people, they used to come in. Another guy named Red Dillon. He was... Phew! Dangerous man. But he used to come in there. See, they had a cook in there named Adele, and everybody loved her cooking.
At Minton’s. So they’d come in and eat.
Fish and chicken. She could cook. She was a good cook.
Were meals on the house, or did you have to pay for them?
No, we had to pay for them! Wasn’t no meals on the house.
I’m actually surprised. Don’t know why, but...
No meals on the house then.
